adapter: quadratic: <scratch>/fresh/quadratic/repo/rsi6/environments/quadratic.py with manifests/quadratic.json and data/quadratic/ (Biq Mac Library, Biq part: beasley, gka, be; 150 instances)
statement: The adapter itself is sound. It reads the Biq Mac sparse files the right way: an entry (i, j) with i < j stands for both q_ij and q_ji. The library's own .mat files confirm this reading, and so does a descent test, which reaches every published value tested and never goes below one. It takes the 150 optimal values exactly as biqmaclib.tex prints them, in the library's minimisation convention, and leaves out the 15 rows that give only bounds. Its evaluation of x'Qx agrees exactly with an independent evaluator on complete answers, on partial totals and on the fast candidate changes. It contains no search, no ranking and no table beyond the instance, and it exposes only Q (diagonal in var_attr, off-diagonal part in var_var). Nothing the learner can observe changes when the reference values are changed. Relabelling is per instance and is decoded correctly. The score is exact, closed-form and monotone in x'Qx, and every malformed answer scores 0. The threshold, however, must not be read the way its anchor suggests. On the kernel's confirming half, which is be200.3 alone, one plain one-flip descent from a random answer already scores 0.97 to 0.98. Plain search with 30 random restarts on the exposed matrix, which the meter does not charge, scores 0.977 on the deciding half and 0.999 on the confirming half. So reaching 0.97 on this category shows nothing beyond plain search, and only the gka-b set (9 of the 24 fresh instances) separates procedures. Separately, the be sets share one generator stream per seed number across sets, and so across the split and across the two halves. These instances are siblings, not copies: values at the same matrix position agree only at chance level. The adapter can be admitted once the anchor is corrected and the threshold is either set per instance set or dropped as evidence, and once the stream sharing is stated in the module text.
coverage:
What I read: every line of quadratic.py and its manifest; problem.py; environment.py; split, halves, layout and _valid in run.py; fetch.py; genassign.py and its manifest; jobshop.py; test_kernel.py; the quadratic section and generator parameters of the pinned biqmaclib.tex; the pinned biqmaclib.html.

What I ran: all scripts are in <scratch>/fresh/quadratic/audit1, run one at a time as instructed, about 30 CPU-seconds in all.
- own.py: my own line-based parser of the sparse files, my own regexes for the tex, and an exact evaluator and score in Python integers and Fractions. It shares no code with the adapter.
- hashes.py: SHA-256 of all 152 manifest files against disk. All 152 equal, none missing, none extra, URLs consistent with paths.
- reading.py: compares four re-fetched files with the manifest, checks five .mat files against the symmetric completion, and runs a 300-start descent under both readings on 21 small instances.
- check1.py: the tables, n, chance and zero values, file form, ranges and densities per set.
- check2.py: evaluator agreement, partial evaluation, the fast rows against the kernel's slow default, relabelling, raw-file order, monkeypatching of the reference, the training flag, degenerate answers, layout, split and halves.
- twins.py, twins2.py, twins3.py: twins across the split and the halves (positional equality, shared 6-value runs, nesting, order patterns).
- order.py: answers hidden in the file order.
- baselines.py and multistart.py: the plain-procedure figures the anchor quotes, and multi-start descent per half.
- final.py: no answer below a published minimum on any of the 150 instances; an answer at the published value scores exactly 1; dtype handling; the view checks.
- tiny.py: metering of the calls; trivial answers by group.

What I fetched: as data only, with curl and the prescribed agent string, into audit1/dl: three folder listings, four re-fetched files and five .mat files.

No learner was constructed. rsi6.kernel.run was imported only for split, halves, layout and _valid.

Not checked:
- The other 115 .mat files (5 of 120 checked).
- Optimality of the published values (not attempted, per the rules).
- The claim that the threshold was fixed before any learner answer was scored (the copy has no ledger).
- Licence statements beyond biqmaclib.html, the tex and the three folder listings.

Side effect, reported: my imports wrote __pycache__ directories into the repo copy. I removed exactly those four directories, and the copy now holds no file newer than the start of the audit.

findings.title: The threshold 0.97 is reached by plain non-learning search, and the anchor says plain procedures stay below it
findings.problem: `anchor` and the 'Threshold 0.97' paragraph say that plain procedures that learn nothing 'stay below it on average' (best-first greedy 0.93, one one-flip descent 0.96). That holds only for single runs, and only as an average over all 150 instances or over the whole fresh side. The kernel scores the deciding half and the confirming half separately against threshold_for = 0.97. The confirming half is be200.3 alone, and on it one one-flip descent from a uniformly random answer already scores 0.974 to 0.983. With a few restarts plain search passes on both halves: the best of 3 descents scores 0.989 on half B, and the best of 30 scores 0.977 on half A and 0.999 on half B. The fresh mean of a single descent stays below 0.97 only because of gka-b (0.66 to 0.74). These procedures run on the exposed var_attr and var_var, where the meter charges only the final construction (n+1 units). That is far below the test-time limit of 41,202 units at n = 200. Reaching the threshold on this category is therefore no evidence of a learned capability, and on half B the confirmation cannot fail for any learner that runs a local search.

findings.fix:
1. In `Quadratic.anchor` and in the module's threshold paragraph, replace the sentence that plain procedures stay below the threshold with the per-half figures:
   - deciding half (be250 and gka-b): one descent about 0.81, best of 3 about 0.91, best of 30 about 0.98;
   - confirming half (be200.3): one descent 0.97 to 0.98, best of 3 0.99, best of 30 1.00.
2. State plainly that on the confirming half a single plain descent reaches the threshold, and that with about 30 restarts computed on the exposed arrays (unmetered) it is reached on both halves.
3. Then do one of the following:
   (a) override threshold_for(instance_ids) so that each scored set gets a threshold above what a pinned plain procedure reaches on that set (for example the best of 3 one-flip descents, measured outside the adapter and tabled in the module text). Even then, no threshold separates search from learning on be200.3, where 30 restarts reach 0.999.
   (b) record in the registration that on this category reaching the threshold is not evidence, and that only the gain counts.

findings.title: The be sets share one generator stream per seed number, across the split and across the halves
findings.problem:
The module says that whole published sets go to one side of the split. That is true, but the sets are not independent: all be classes were generated with seeds 1 to 10, and the files with the same number k share the generator's stream of values.
- Row 1 lists the same value sequence in every such file: be100.1, be200.3.1, be200.8.1 and be250.1 all start -100, -24, 1, 42, -44, -6, and so on.
- The k-th listed value agrees for 41 to 97 percent of the first 2,000 entries.
- For equal n the sparsity patterns are nested.
- Across the split: 10 of the 24 fresh instances share a seed with a training instance. These are be200.3.{1,2,4,5,6,9} and be250.{1,2,4,5}; the training instances are be100.1, be100.9, be120.3.5, be120.8.2, be150.8.2, be150.8.4 and be200.8.6.
- Across the halves: six pairs be250.k (half A) and be200.3.k (half B), for k in {1,2,4,5,7,10}. gka-b (half A, seed 10) also shares the seed-10 stream, under a monotone change of range, with be200.3.10 (half B).
- Values at the same matrix position agree only at chance level, so these are distinct problems and not copies.
The kernel's halves() text asks that instances which share data (a matrix, a generator) not be split, and the bin-packing adapter was required to keep no shared stretch of its stream between training and fresh.
findings.fix:
1. In the Groups paragraph, state that the be files with the same number were made with the same seed and share one generator stream across sets. Say the same of the gka files that share seeds (10, 8, 31, 34 and 47, by the tex parameters). Say also that bqp50 and bqp100 share stretches, which do not cross the present split.
2. List the cross-split and cross-half pairs given above, with the measured figures, and say that the matrices differ entry-wise (about 1 percent positional agreement).
3. If the protocol applies the bin-packing rule to this category, define group() by generator seed instead of by published set: be<...>.k goes to 'seed-k'; gka-a, gka-b and gka1c join seed 10, and gka5c joins seed 8. Instances that share a stream then fall on one side and in one half.

findings.title: The manifest misquotes the gka paragraph of the page
findings.problem: The `terms` field says of the beasley and gka sets that they 'can be obtained from this site or from the OR-Library'. The page says that for beasley. For gka it says 'Also these datasets can be obtained from this website or from the OR-Library'. The rest of the terms statement is accurate as far as the page, the tex and the folder listings show: none of them states a licence or terms of use.
findings.evidence: The pinned biqmaclib.html, as text: beasley 'The datasets can be obtained from this site or from the OR-Library.'; gka 'Also these datasets can be obtained from this website or from the OR-Library.'. The folder listings and the tex contain no licence, copyright or terms wording.
findings.fix: Quote the two sentences separately, or write: 'can be obtained from this site [website] or from the OR-Library'.

evaluator_agreement:
My own parser, evaluator and score were written from the page and tex text and share no code with the adapter. The parser is line-based and keeps the entries as Python integers. The evaluator computes x'Qx as the sum over listed entries of q*x_i*x_j, counting off-diagonal entries twice; the score is an exact Fraction.

Complete answers: 384 answers on 12 instances from 12 sets (bqp50-1, bqp250-3, gka1b, gka10b, gka3c, gka5d, gka2e, gka8a, be100.1, be200.8.4, be250.7, be200.3.5). Per instance: 30 random answers of random density, plus all-zero and all-one, given in the relabelled problem and decoded. The adapter's score() equals my exact score to within 1e-15, and both P.evaluate() and view(P).evaluate() equal my integer value exactly: 0 disagreements.

Partial evaluation: 7 instances, 3 random trajectories each, 276 partial states and 6,624 candidate entries covering both assigned and unassigned variables. candidates() equals the difference of my own partial totals every time. After every assign, totals() equals both partial_totals() and my partial total, and the final totals() equals evaluate(). The fast rows equal the kernel's slow default AssignProblem._rows on 5 instances, including the state with all variables assigned.

References: my regexes find 165 table rows: 150 with an optimum and 15 with bounds only (bqp500-1..10, gka1f..5f). All 150 values equal the adapter's references. n, the chance values and the zero points are exactly equal (compared as Fractions). The adapter's dense Q equals the symmetric completion of my parse on all 150 instances.

Reading of the files: the library's .mat files for gka1b, gka3b, gka2c, be120.3.1 and be200.3.1 equal the symmetric completion, not the upper triangle. A 300-start descent under the symmetric reading reaches the published value on all 21 instances tested and never goes below it. Under the reading where each listed entry counts once, the descent goes below the published minimum on gka1b, gka2b, gka3b and gka4b (gka1b: -154 against -133; gka3b: -134 against -118).

Reference answers: the source publishes values only, no solution vectors. A 30-start descent found no answer below a published minimum on any of the 150 instances and reached the published value on 90 of them. Answers at the published value score exactly 1.0, both directly and through relabel and decode.
exposed:
Every array the problem object exposes, and where it comes from:
- var_attr, shape (n, 1): q_ii, the file's entry (i, i), or 0 if the file lists none. Checked equal to my own parse after the relabelling permutation.
- var_var[0], shape (n, n): q_ij for i != j, the file's entry (min(i,j), max(i,j)), placed symmetrically, with a zero diagonal. Checked equal to my symmetric completion, relabelled. The symmetric reading is confirmed by the .mat files and by the descent test.
- opt_attr, shape (2, 0): empty.
- opt_opt, var_opt, occ_attr: empty.
- groups: one group; hard [False], detail [False]. It is the partial x'Qx (terms whose variables are all at 1), which is exact and specified.
- capacity, domain, start_answer, start_totals: None. ordered: False.
- n_vars: the file's n. n_opts: 2.

The adapter's problem object also holds diag, which equals var_attr. It carries no name, no reference and no chance value. Pickles of the problem and of the view are byte-identical when the stored best, chance and zero values are changed, and between training=True and training=False. No reference value, negated or halved reference, chance value or zero point occurs in any exposed array.

Design decisions that shape difficulty:
- The answer form is the specification's own: every x in {0,1}^n is an answer, with no decoding rule and no hard group. Options are not relabelled; option 0 never changes the total.
- Exposing the whole of Q gives the learner the complete objective. It can evaluate any answer or flip itself on these arrays, and the meter charges only calls, so search on them is bounded by CPU, not by units.
- candidates() on assigned variables returns the exact one-flip changes of a complete answer at 2 units per variable. This is the kernel's default meaning, not an addition.
- The zero point min(chance, 0) departs from the work order's chance-only zero point, for a documented and correct reason: with the chance value alone, x = 0 would score 0.969 to 0.999 on gka-b. It is exact and closed-form, and it does not read the reference. Its effect is that gka-b becomes a plain ratio scale, on which the no-search answer 'only the variable with the most negative q_ii' scores 0.457 on average.
- On degenerate answers: all-zero scores 0 everywhere. All-ones is valid and scores up to 0.44 (gka5c), with a mean of 0.082; every malformed or degenerate answer tried scores 0.
- The kernel's split puts gka-b, whose off-diagonal entries are all positive and which is unlike every training set, only on the fresh side.
- File order hides no answer. The ones of the published-value answers show no positional bias (|rank z| at most 1.33 on 14 instances). The best prefix or suffix answer scores a mean of 0.212 in file order against 0.210 after relabelling. Relabelling permutes the rows and columns of Q jointly, and two seeds give different orders.
